title: Uniform laws never force the knot's contradiction
claim: A law of lines and co-lines, in which each corner of a line lies in exactly one co-line and each point's link alternates lines and co-lines in one cycle, builds its own closed surface. (1) The Cayley law C(G; x, y) - points G, lines {g, gx, gxy}, co-lines the cosets of <x>, <y>, <(xy)^-1> - is always such a law, orientable, with every point of co-line sizes (|x|, |y|, |xy|). (2) If every point of a law has co-line sizes (d1, d2, d3), then chi = n(1/d1 + 1/d2 + 1/d3 - 1), so the law closes into a sphere only for (2,2,d) with n = 2d, (2,3,3) with n = 12, (2,3,4) with n = 24 and (2,3,5) with n = 60 - the antiprisms and the snub polyhedra, realized on dihedral groups, A4, S4 and A5. (3) With uniform signs (every line the same pattern) every even co-line is an even face, so chi - |D| <= n(sum over odd sizes of 1/d - 1) <= 0: the count never forces the knot's lines to fail on any uniform law, and on uniform spheres it forces over-agreement instead. (4) With Kasteleyn signs, which are not uniform on spheres, the knot fails on every uniform sphere, but only on at most 60 points or on an antiprism, a cyclic chain on which binary search finds a violated line with O(log n) queries. (5) Computed: with uniform signs the knot is satisfiable on every tested uniform law and on every circulant law with n <= 48 except the Fano plane; the knot sphere K_k has exactly two kinds of points.
failure_conditions: A Cayley law that is not a closed orientable surface, or whose Euler characteristic differs from the formula.
A uniform signing under which the count forces a line to fail, or an even co-line that is not an even face.
A uniform sphere whose knot is satisfiable under Kasteleyn signs, or an antiprism law that is not a cyclic chain of width 1.
A tested uniform law with uniform signs whose knot is unsatisfiable, other than the Fano plane.
foundation_claim_scope: (1)-(4) for every finite group and every law of one point type, by proof; computed on V4, D_3..D_12, A4, S4, A5, wallpaper quotients of types (3,3,3), (2,4,4), (2,3,6), PSL(2,7) and all circulant laws with n <= 48; the knot sphere's point types for k = 2..6.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: by hand; finite claims checked by computation with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: the curvature formula and the spherical list are the classical classification of vertex-transitive maps (the antiprisms and snub polyhedra; Cayley maps of (2,3,n) triangle-group quotients); new as far as found: the reading of a knot law with its co-lines as a self-built surface, the theorem that uniform signs never let the count force the knot's lines, and the bound on the depth of uniform contradictions.
